pr_title: [Subtitles] Show font family name's to subtitle fonts list
pr_body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->
This change allow to show in the subtitles font setting list, the font family name instead of the font filename, as happens on every text editor.
To achieve this has been introduced a new building fonts cache which is triggered when Kodi is started. This also solves the side effect of the GUI freeze every time you try to open the subtitle Kodi settings when there are hundreds/thousands of fonts,
and ensure to fix #20861 memory leak.

## Motivation and context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
Initially started to fix issue #20861 for a memory leak,
i preferred to make more radical changes in order to improve the current architecture.

The memory leak was because `ass_set_fonts` was called more times,
and libass was not cleaningup the allocated memory, libass bug!?

The choice to call `ass_set_fonts` each time the style change was made for two main reasons:
- be able to set the selected font from our fonts folders (kodi system or user), this was a kind of workaround to manage fonts from more folders, thing not supported from libass (allow only one additional folder)
- was not implemented a way to get the font family name, kodi only provided the font filename
with the side effect in some cases to have the font provider disabled in libass.

Then implementing a way to retrieve the font family name,
allow to set the right font name to the libass style, avoid call `ass_set_fonts` each time (then no mem leak),
and allowing the advantage to have a font list with font family names in font settings.

To note that the default subtitle font, is now called as:
`Default DejaVu Sans`
this is a dynamic entry constructed by code, in two string parts:
"Default" + font family name, of the default kodi font file set by source code

Why the default Kodi font is not more called `Arial`?
As someone has tried to explain in this issue #19912, our current default Kodi font used in GUI and subtitles, is a real chimera,
the Arial name come from first Kodi versions (10.0 ?) but has nothing to do with Arial font, appears to be a merge of two differents fonts: DejaVu Sans + Droid Sans Fallback, no longer up-to-date.
After the future merge of GUI font rework PR, we are planning to remove this chimera Arial font

## How has this been tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your change. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
Load more than 1000 fonts in user fonts folder
Load some SRT subtitle and look at loaded font name in libass log
Test an ASS subtitle for testing various overriding settings

I've already "looked" into it trying to picture something that could be extendable, abstract and benefit Kodi as whole, unfortunately it involves a bit of effort and small steps:

- Kill `g_FontManager` global, move it to the service broker
- Ideally some other component should be the parent of fontmanager, something similar to what we have for GUI (we have GUIComponent that is the parent of some other GUI related objects). This helps making building blocks and get a better picture of the application as a whole. Since Fonts are resources and might be available even if kodi is running headless (e.g. you could have subtitles in the webinterface using the same fonts you'd have in the GUI player), I'd go with `CResources` or something similar. `CResources` would hold the FontManager object and initialize it. The component itself is initialized from CApp.
- Skins should be removed from CApp and moved to a `SkinManager` element that is a child of `CGUIComponent`
- There are a lot of components that can provide fonts. We could have some sort of abstraction `CFontProvider` as a sort of abstract base class. This abstract class registers on `FontManager` as a provider with a given ID on construction/initialization and de-registers itself on destruction/deinitialization. Virtual methods for FontLoading, FontData loading, etc.
- Skins are fontproviders, should use it as a base
- Font addons are fontproviders, should use it as a base
- In the future, script addons that provides skin elements can also be font providers solving one of the issues that have always affected addons (they can't use custom fonts)
- The mkv demuxer is also a font provider
- etc,

In this concrete example, the demuxer would derive from `FontProvider` and load (`std::move`) transitory/temporary font data to the font manager. The libass handler (`CDVDLibass`) would then use the broker to get the resource component, from there the fontmanager, and move the transitory font data again into memory.

Just some thoughts. And yeap, it involves quite a bit of work - feel free to disagree or propose something different. That's the reason I still think my commit above, while not solving this for the long term, is still an intermediary solution that would allow us to cleanup the `temp` hack in libass and fontmanager while allowing us to move forward with some other alternative in the future.

[Kodi 20] Changing subtitles appearance when subtitles's showing during video playback,

( Sorry for my ENG, I'm not native. )

A system with low free memory like android tv box began to stutter to crash with several repeated attempts.

<!--- Put your text below this line -->

Sorry, I don't know.

yes a kind of workaround, not perfect because `ConfigureFont` wrapped by the condition `if (m_subtitleType == ADAPTED || ....` can be not always executed
but however, we are already doing some workarounds around the font handling,
begins to be a mess, i do not know, i do not like too much...
before i couldn't find anything better, but now i have a new idea to avoid all this

Current problems:
1) libass support to load fonts from 1 additional folder only (set by `ass_set_fonts_dir`), plus, is possible add 1 font fallback that can be on a different folder. But kodi have 2 additionals folders (kodi app font folder + user font folder) by default we set the user folder, then if you try to use a font from app folder, the font will not works.
2) The kodi subtitle font setting menu, show the font list (and save) the -file name- of the font. But libass `style->FontName` require the real font name, not the file name. This prevent libass to find in right way the font.

To fix these problems in the past i was add the `ConfigureFont` as workaround, to call `ass_set_fonts` at each time the font name change and by forcing fontprovider disabled to force libass load the font where we want, but with the side effect that with fontprovider disabled should not allow font fallbacks to system font provider.

This is my idea to remove the workarounds and handle the font in better way, avoid also to disable font provider:
- Remove `ConfigureFont`
- Set `ass_set_fonts` in the libass class initialization by adding "Arial" as additional font fallback from kodi app font folder
- On `ass_set_fonts_dir` we set the kodi app font folder, but if the user folder contains files we set instead the user font folder (in this way we should allow libass to use all kodi fonts as fallback, if the user not add his custom fonts)
- On `style->FontName` we have to set the real font name, in kodi we have the freetype library, in theory we can use it to retrieve the real font name from the selected file.
- On the kodi subtitle font setting list, we have to avoid load the fonts from kodi app font folder. Then we will add only the fallback "Arial" font + all the fonts in the user font folder
